This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.274/2019, registered at P.S.- Baikunthpur,
District- Rewa (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(i), 506, 376(3) & 450 of IPC,
and under Section 3, 4, 5j(ii) and 6 of POCSO Act.
He is in detention since 25.02.2022.
Applicant's first application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 20.09.2022.
As per the prosecution story, on 12.10.2019 prosecutrix lodged an FIR in P.S Baikunthpur, Rewa alleging that she has studied upto class 5th and her parents are labourers.

sentences.text: In March, 2019 Gabbar was in her village.
On 15.03.2019, when parents of the prosecutrix had gone for wages and she was alone at home, Gabbar made a call through the phone of Ravi and after that he came to her house.

She asked him not to come as her parents were not at home but at around 7 PM, Gabbar came inside her home, closed the doors from inside and forcibly laid her on the ground and committed rape upon her.
He had threatened to kill her if she discloses the incident to anyone.
Now she is carrying pregnancy and has informed her parents about the incident.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Prosecutrix was a consenting party and same can be inferred from her evidence before the trial Court.
Learned counsel for the applicant has referred para 5 and 6 and subsequent para of cross-examination of the prosecutrix and on aforesaid pretext he has prayed that applicant be released on bail.
In DNA report, applicant has been found to be biological father of the child delivered by the prosecutrix.
Prosecutrix has been consistent and firm in her FIR, statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C and even in the Court evidence that it was the present applicant who had committed rape upon her.

Therefore, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on merit of the case, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of bail.
Therefore, this second bail application under section 439 of Cr.P.C filed on behalf of applicant Gabbar Singh Kol is dismissed.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE anu Gabbar Singh Kol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154889826/
